title: An Enhanced Data Packing Method for General Matrix Multiplication in Brakerski/Fan-Vercauteren Scheme
problem: Performing GEMM in Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is inefficient due to high computational demands, significant data migration bandwidth constraints, and incompatibility of standard activation functions with FHE schemes like BFV.
motivation: FHE enables privacy-preserving ML inference but bandwidth and computation overhead limit practical deployment; efficient GEMM packing under BFV scheme is key bottleneck for FHE-based ML acceleration.
method: The paper uses polynomial encoding—a technique for packing encrypted numbers into polynomials so computation can happen on encrypted data—to perform matrix multiplication under the Brakerski/Fan-Vercauteren homomorphic encryption scheme. It shows how to pack multiple matrix inputs and weights into these polynomials efficiently, regardless of matrix size. To speed this up, it designs custom hardware on an FPGA (the U250 chip) that works together with the main computer, dividing computation so each handles what it does best.
key_novelty: It performs encrypted matrix multiplication using polynomial encoding in the Brakerski/Fan-Vercauteren scheme, combined with FPGA hardware (U250) that optimizes work division between the accelerator and host computer.
contributions: Polynomial encoding methodology for BFV GEMM with variable sizes
4.22x speedup on MNIST vs. existing solutions
limitations: Evaluation limited to MNIST and CIFAR-10; scalability to larger models and other FHE schemes not discussed.
primary_theme: polynomial-encoded GEMM for FHE-based ML inference
